pamphlet_excerpts: Water and Bodily Functions: Water is essential for nearly every bodily function (p. 48).
Causes of Trail Dehydration: People who lose more water than they take in risk becoming dehydrated (p. 48).
Early Signs of Dehydration: The first sign of dehydration usually is dark urine (p. 48).
Systemic Symptoms of Fluid Loss: Other signs can include weariness, headache, body aches, and confusion (p. 48).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Monitor Urine Color Regularly: The first sign of dehydration usually is dark urine (p. 48).
Step 2 - Recognize Dehydration Warning Signs: Other signs can include weariness, headache, body aches, and confusion (p. 48).
Step 3 - Assess Temperature Related Illnesses: Heat exhaustion, heatstroke, and hypothermia might all be caused in part by dehydration (p. 48).
Step 4 - Drink Fluids Before Thirst: Prevent dehydration and heat reactions by drinking plenty of fluids (p. 48).

pamphlet_excerpts: Environmental Stewardship on Trails: Caring for the environment is an important responsibility of every hiker (p. 28).
Leave No Trace Foundations: Leave No Trace is just one set of principles that can help you live up to that responsibility and enjoy the outdoors fully by knowing (p. 28).
Group Trip Planning Ethics: As you and your group plan a hike, ask yourselves how you can follow each of the principles of Leave No Trace (p. 28).
Respecting Nature and Others: Leave No Trace and The Outdoor Code are principles that help you respect the environment and be considerate to others who are enjoying the outdoors (p. 28).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Plan Low Impact Routes: As you and your group plan a hike, ask yourselves how you can follow each of the principles of Leave No Trace (p. 28).
Step 2 - Practice Trail Courtesy Daily: Leave No Trace and The Outdoor Code are principles that help you respect the environment and be considerate to others who are enjoying the outdoors (p. 28).
Step 3 - Review Route With Leaders: Explain your desired route and ask how you can best implement Leave No Trace (p. 28).
Step 4 - Follow Backcountry Stewardship Guidelines: Here are some additional guidelines to remember (p. 28).

pamphlet_excerpts: Risks of Unprepared Hiking: Setting off on a hike without properly preparing can have disastrous results (p. 33).
Physical Readiness and Gear: Make sure you are ready, from your physical condition to the best gear for the trip (p. 33).
Fitness for Trail Enjoyment: To enjoy hiking to the fullest, you will want to be in good shape (p. 33).
Structured Personal Conditioning Plans: That is why requirement 3 calls for developing a plan for conditioning yourself (p. 33).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Build Baseline Aerobic Fitness: To enjoy hiking to the fullest, you will want to be in good shape (p. 33).
Step 2 - Design a Conditioning Schedule: That is why requirement 3 calls for developing a plan for conditioning yourself (p. 33).
Step 3 - Increase Trail Mileage Gradually: Begin with short trips, increasing the length of your journeys as you become more fit (p. 33).

File a detailed trip plan with a responsible adult, carry the Scout Basic Essentials, wear broken-in footwear with synthetic or wool socks, pace the group to the slowest hiker using the buddy system, treat foot hot spots immediately, and turn back from exposed ridges before afternoon lightning storms build.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. File a detailed trip plan with a responsible adult, carry the Scout Basic Essentials, wear broken-in footwear with synthetic or wool socks, pace the group to the slowest hiker using the buddy system, treat foot hot spots immediately, and turn back from exposed ridges before afternoon lightning storms build.

D. Relying strictly on high-energy trail snacks to substitute for physical conditioning.
choices: A. Running a single 20-mile marathon the day before your first merit badge hike.
B. Walking daily instead of riding in cars whenever possible, beginning with short trips, and gradually increasing distance as you get fitter.
C. Lifting heavy weights once a month while avoiding all outdoor walking to save energy for the trail.
